newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Britain's Blair a Peronist, says Argentine senator.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Blair a Peronist, says Argentine senator.

text.p: A Peronist senator said Friday that British Prime Minister Tony Blair sounded like Gen. Juan Peron, the populist leader who nationalised British companies in Argentina five decades ago.
Sen. Antonio Cafiero said Blair's recent call for a "third way" between old socialist statism and market liberalism in Europe was an example of the policies espoused by Peron.
"Peron launched the third position half a century ago, in the post-war era," Cafiero wrote in a newspaper column. The "third way" was to steer between capitalism and socialism.
"Tony Blair probably was not inspired by Peron. But he repeats his ideas and has made them his hallmark," Cafiero said in the column published by the nespaper El Clarin.
Peron, whose wife Evita was immortalised in musicals and more recently on screen by pop star Madonna, was president of Argentina from 1946-55 and from 1973 to his death in 1974.
Blair led Britain's Labour Party to victory in May by guiding the party away from its old socialist tenets of high taxation and the nationalisation of private firms.
